resources.string: From heartbeat signal to muscle contraction
Electrical signal
A simplified diagram of normal cardiac conduction and a ventricular muscle cell. Paths, timing and shortening are illustrative, not ECG or personal measurements.
The sinoatrial node starts the beat
Specialized pacemaker cells start an electrical signal. It spreads through the atria, helping them contract.
The atrioventricular node slows the signal
Conduction through the atrioventricular node takes longer. This timing lets the atria contract before the ventricles do.
The signal reaches the ventricles
The signal follows the bundle and its branches, then the Purkinje fibers rapidly distribute it through the ventricles.
Calcium helps the muscle cell shorten
When a ventricular muscle cell is excited, a small influx of calcium triggers more calcium release from internal stores. Calcium enables the contractile filaments to slide past each other.
Calcium falls and the muscle relaxes
Calcium is moved back into internal stores or out of the cell. As cytoplasmic calcium falls, the filaments relax and the muscle can lengthen again.
